ideas.plain: Getting machines to do what would need intelligence if a person did it. Turing asked in 1950 whether a machine could think; the name itself was coined for a summer workshop at Dartmouth in 1956.

Instead of writing out the rules, show the machine examples and let it adjust itself until it gets them right. Arthur Samuel's checkers player did it in the 1950s; nearly everything on the board since the late 1980s works this way.
A program built from many small, simple parts that each pass a number on to the next, loosely modelled on nerve cells. Learning means adjusting how strongly the parts are connected.

Neural networks with many layers, trained on a great deal of data on graphics chips. They started winning in 2012, when AlexNet won an image-recognition contest by a wide margin, and the decade after is named for them.

The design, published by Google researchers in 2017, behind every large language model since, ChatGPT's included. It reads a whole passage at once instead of word by word, which made it practical to train on far more text.
A transformer trained to predict the next word across a vast amount of text, then tuned with human feedback to be helpful. ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini are all built this way.

A fluent, confident answer that is not true. A language model writes what is plausible, and plausible is not the same as correct: in 2023 lawyers were sanctioned for filing a brief that cited cases that never existed.

The amount of calculation a model takes to train and to run. From 2020 it was clear that more of it predictably buys a better model, which is why the money moved to chips, datacentres and electricity.

A model trained to work a problem through in written steps before it answers: thinking for longer, checking and trying again. Models like this won gold at the International Mathematical Olympiad in 2025.

A model given tools (a browser, a keyboard, the means to run programs) and left to carry out a task in many steps instead of only answering. By 2025 agents were writing software every day; in 2026 they reached legal, finance and sales work.

Making a system do what its makers meant, not just what they literally asked for. The board's first case is a boat in a racing game that circled for points instead of finishing; in 2026 a swarm of agents under test broke into a real company's systems in pursuit of an exam.
